primary_source_citation.title: FAA Pilot's Handbook (FAA-H-8083-25C Ch. 5) Technical Reference: Four Forces of Flight & Three-Axis Primary Flight Controls

1.rule_of_thumb_mnemonic: In steady unaccelerated level flight, Lift equals Weight and Thrust equals Drag; exceeding critical angle of attack (~16-18 deg) triggers an aerodynamic stall.
core_mechanism_bullets: 1. Lift vs. Weight (Vertical Axis): Curved upper camber accelerates airflow (Bernoulli lower pressure) while downward trailing wash (Newton 3rd Law) generates upward Lift.
2. Thrust vs. Drag (Longitudinal Axis): Propeller or turbofan accelerates air rearward to overcome parasite form drag and lift-induced wingtip vortex drag.
3. Roll (Ailerons) & Pitch (Elevator): Moving yoke left/right moves outboard wing ailerons oppositely to Roll; pulling yoke aft raises tail Elevator to Pitch nose up.
4. Yaw (Rudder Pedals) & Coordinated Turn: Foot pedals deflect vertical tail Rudder left/right around the vertical axis to counter adverse yaw and keep the inclinometer ball centered.

Step 2: Apply the field rule of thumb (In steady unaccelerated level flight, Lift equals Weight and Thrust equals Drag; exceeding critical angle of attack (~16-18 deg) triggers an aerodynamic stall.). Step 3: Verify each measurement or checkpoint against FAA Pilot's Handbook (FAA-H-8083-25C Ch. 5) reference criteria and record your findings in your Scout Workbook.

primary_source_citation.title: FAA Pilot's Handbook (FAA-H-8083-25C Ch. 8) Technical Reference: The Cockpit 'Six-Pack': Pitot-Static vs. Gyroscopic Instruments

2.rule_of_thumb_mnemonic: 3 Pitot-Static instruments measure air pressure (ASI, Altimeter, VSI); 3 Gyroscopic instruments measure spin inertia (Attitude, Heading, Turn Coordinator).
core_mechanism_bullets: Pitot + Static: Airspeed Indicator (Knots): Subtracts static port pressure from forward ram-air Pitot pressure; color arcs mark white flap range, green normal, yellow caution, red Vne.
Static Pressure: Altimeter & VSI: Aneroid wafers expand as ambient pressure drops with altitude (~1 inHg per 1,000 ft), driving the 3-pointer Altimeter and ft/min VSI.
Gyroscopic: Attitude & Heading Indicators: Artificial horizon shows real-time bank angle and pitch relative to horizon; Heading Indicator tracks magnetic compass heading.
Engine & Tachometer Monitoring: RPM tachometer, oil temperature, and oil pressure gauges give immediate early warning of powerplant anomalies.

primary_source_citation.title: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook (FAA-H-8083-3C) Technical Reference: Cessna 172 Walk-Around Preflight & Runway Magnetic Numbering

3.rule_of_thumb_mnemonic: Runway numbers drop the last digit of magnetic compass heading: Runway 27 points due West (270 degrees magnetic); planes take off and land INTO the wind.
core_mechanism_bullets: Cockpit Safety & A-R-R-O-W Check: Verify Magnetos OFF, Master switch OFF, control lock removed, and Airworthiness, Registration, Radio, Operating Handbook, Weight & Balance.
Fuel Sump Drain & Quantity Check: Visually dip both wing tanks and drain low-point fuel sumps into a clear tester cup to verify zero water globules or debris.
Airframe, Hinges, Pitot & Prop Walk-Around: Remove red 'Remove Before Flight' Pitot cover, inspect propeller leading edge for nicks, check tire inflation, and test all control hinges.
Runway Markings, Windsock & Phonetic ATC: Read windsock direction to pick the headwind runway, hold short of double solid/dashed yellow lines, and use ICAO Alpha-Bravo-Charlie radio calls.

primary_source_citation.title: FAA STEM AVSED & EAA Young Eagles Technical Reference: Aviation & Aerospace Career Pathways, FAA Certificates & STEM Roles

4.rule_of_thumb_mnemonic: You can solo a glider at age 14, solo a powered airplane at age 16, and take an EAA Young Eagles introductory flight today for $0.
core_mechanism_bullets: 1. FAA Pilot Certificate Ladder: Student Pilot solo at 16 (glider at 14) -> Private Pilot (PPL) at 17 -> Instrument Rating (IFR) -> Commercial (CPL) -> Airline Transport (ATP).
2. Airframe & Powerplant (A&P) Mechanic: FAA-certificated aviation maintenance technicians inspect turbines, avionics, hydraulics, and structural composites before every flight.
3. FAA Air Traffic Controller (ATC): Tower, TRACON approach, and En Route center controllers sequence thousands of daily flights safely through radar and ADS-B separation.
4. Aerospace & Unmanned Systems Engineer: Designs wings, propulsion, fly-by-wire avionics, autonomous Part 107 drones, and spacecraft in wind tunnels and CFD simulators.
